description: Word goes down Sprocket Row faster than the Post: No. 9 is let again. By noon your neighbours on the Row have found reasons to pass your window, and then reasons to stop at it. You give them something to watch, and hang your tools on the hooks above the bench. Behind the last hook, pushed into the gap against the wall, is a notebook's binding: marbled boards, a cloth spine, H. Vane inked inside the front board in a small upright hand. You take it down. Every page has been torn out at the stitching. "She was never without that," says someone at the window. Someone else wants to know whether you are stopping.

options.label: Prop the door open and let the neighbours look their fill.

success.text: By teatime the Row has decided you are thin, clever and probably not stopping, and the pie shop sends round a pie to test at least the first. A neighbour looks over the Boiler that runs your workshop and gives you her opinion of it. It is not high, but it is free, and she is right about the feed pump.

options.label: Shut the door and chalk a sign on it: CLOSED FOR REPAIRS. OPINIONS BY APPOINTMENT.

success.text: The sign is read aloud the length of the Row before the chalk is dry, and improved twice by morning. Nobody calls. But the next day there is a tin of good oil on your step, with no note, and you understand that the Row has decided to wait and see. That is as close to a welcome as Sprocket Row gives anyone.
